figures.caption: Fig. 3 (a) Interfacial degradation at the cathode interface occurring at high SOC, illustrating oxygen release from the delithiated cathode and its reaction with sulfide SEs, leading to interfacial decomposition and rock- salt layer formation. Reproduced with permission from ref. 57. Copyright 2025, Elsevier. (b) Pseudo-binary phase diagram between LPSCl and delithiated NCA, indicating their thermodynamic incompatibility and the spontaneous formation of decomposition products. (c) Atomic structure of a half-charged NCA/LPSCl interface at 50 ps calculated by ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), showing interfacial reconstruction and the formation of decomposition species such as LiCl, Li3PO4, and NiS2. Reproduced with permission from ref. 51. Copyright 2019, American Chemical Society.

figures.caption: Fig. 4 (a) ToF-SIMS measurements for cycled and uncycled composite cathodes with and without VGCF, showing increased phosphate-related fragment intensity in carbon-containing electrodes, indicative of accelerated SE decomposition. Reproduced with permission from ref. 71. Copyright 2020, American Chemical Society. (b) Eﬀect of CA on the decomposition of SEs, illustrating enhanced electron leakage and decomposition reactions at the TPB with increasing carbon content. Reproduced with permission from ref. 69. Copyright 2024, Wiley-VCH GmbH.

Reproduced with permission from ref. 81. Copyright 2016, Elsevier. (c) Diﬀerent types of Li metal–SE interfaces, illustrating the classification into stable, MIEC, and passivating SEI-forming interfaces and their distinct interfacial evolution behaviors. figures.caption: Fig. 6 (a) Voltage versus time for a Li|LPSCl|Li cell, plated at a current density of 3.0 mA cm2, showing sudden voltage drop associated with filamentary conduction and short-circuiting. (b) Operando XCT images showing the growth of a crack through an initially pristine SE with Li penetration along defects and grain boundaries. Reproduced with permis- sion from ref. 89. Copyright 2023, Springer Nature. (c) SEI layer formation at the Li/LPS interface. Reproduced with permission from ref. 90. Copy- right 2025, Wiley-VCH GmbH.

figures.caption: Fig. 7 (a) Morphological structural changes in a composite cathode by the application of fabrication pressure, illustrating the formation of inter- facial voids arising from particle size mismatch and non-uniform stress distribution. Pressure-dependent (b) porosity, contact area fraction, and charge/discharge curves at 0.01C, showing that increased pressure reduces porosity, enhances interfacial contact, and improves electroche- mical performance. Reproduced from ref. 99 under the terms of the CC BY 3.0 license. Copyright 2020, Royal Society of Chemistry.

figures.caption: Fig. 8 (a) Discharge capacity of the cell before and after re-pressing, showing partial recovery of discharge capacity achieved by re-establishing physical contact. (b) Cell resistances determined through EIS measure- ments, indicating a significant increase in interfacial resistance during cycling and its reduction after re-pressing. Reproduced from ref. 105 under the terms of the CC BY-NC 3.0 license. Copyright 2020, Royal Society of Chemistry.

figures.caption: Fig. 9 (a) 3D rendering of the tomographic data over the high-nickel NCM secondary particle, illustrating crack initiation and propagation within the particle. (b) Evolution of Li concentration and the damage along the grain boundaries, showing the preferentially localized damage at grain boundaries. Reproduced from ref. 111 under the terms of the CC BY 4.0 license. Copyright 2020 The Authors, published by Springer Nature. (c) Morphological change of the single- and poly-crystalline high-nickel NCM cathode during pressing and cycling, highlighting severe intergranular cracking in polycrystalline particles and enhanced structural stability in single-crystalline counterparts. Reproduced with permission from ref. 114. Copyright 2021, Wiley-VCH GmbH.
figures.src: 01. Intertwined nature of electrochemical reactions and mechanical instability in sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries.pdf

figures.caption: Fig. 10 (a) Interface pore formation during stripping at an incoherent interface, illustrating the nucleation and growth of voids due to Li vacancy accumulation. Reproduced with permission from ref. 117. Copyright 2021, Wiley-VCH GmbH. (b) Li/LPSCl interface cycled above the critical stripping current density, showing progressive void coalescence and interfacial instability during repeated plating/stripping. (c) SEM cross-sections of the Li/LPSCl interface, revealing the evolution of voids, crack propagation, and severe interfacial degradation with cycling. Reproduced with permission from ref. 118. Copyright 2019, Springer Nature.
figures.src: 01. Intertwined nature of electrochemical reactions and mechanical instability in sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries.pdf

figures.caption: Fig. 11 (a) Stress distribution at an 80% discharged state for various NCM-to-SE ratios, showing the development of localized stress concentrations with increasing microstructural inhomogeneity. (b) FIB-SEM images of composite cathodes with NCM-to-SE ratios of 70 : 30, 80 : 20, 85 : 15. Reproduced with permission from ref. 37. Copyright 2025, American Chemical Society. (c) Comparison of the volumetric strain, von Mises stress, and crack order between case 1 (inhomogeneous) and case 2 (homogeneous), demonstrating that structural inhomogeneity leads to heterogeneous stress distribution and accelerated crack propagation. Reproduced with permission from ref. 39. Copyright 2025, Elsevier.
figures.src: 01. Intertwined nature of electrochemical reactions and mechanical instability in sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries.pdf

figures.caption: Fig. 12 (a) In situ pressure measurement curves and voltage profiles of the Li–In cell and LTO cell, showing significantly larger pressure fluctua- tions in Li–In cells due to high-strain anode behavior. (b) XPS spectra obtained from the cathodes Li–In cell and LTO cell before after cycling. (c) Cross-sectional SEM images of the cathodes collected before and after cycling, revealing severe intergranular cracking and structural degradation in Li–In cells. (d) Schematic illustration of the anode-derived chemo- mechanical degradation of the cathode, highlighting stress transfer, dynamic interface evolution, and resulting heterogeneity-induced crack- ing. Reproduced with permission from ref. 32. Copyright 2023, Elsevier.

figures.caption: Fig. 13 (a) Critical current density tests of sulfide SE symmetric cells, showing enhanced critical current density upon borohydride doping. (b) Borohydride doping eﬀect on the properties of Li/SE interphases, illustrating the formation of a thin, mechanically compliant, and electronically insulating SEI that stabilizes Li plating/stripping. Reproduced from ref. 127 under the terms of the CC BY 4.0 license. Copyright 2025 The Authors, published by Wiley-VCH GmbH. (c) Crystal structure of O-doped argyrodite SEs. (d) Cyclic voltammetry tests for C + SE|SE|Li cells, showing an expanded electrochemical stability window with suppressed decomposition reactions. (e) Li3PO4 as a buﬀer layer at the cathode interface. Reproduced with permission from ref. 128. Copyright 2022, Wiley-VCH GmbH.

figures.caption: Fig. 14 (a) STEM-HAADF images of NCM particle with a conformal LZC coating layer. (b) Interfacial reactions between the NCM and LPSCl, illustrating the suppression of resistive interlayer formation by surface coating. (c) Cycling performances of ASSBs with NCM and NCM@LZC, demonstrating improved capacity retention upon interface stabilization. Reproduced with permission from ref. 137. Copyright 2024, Elsevier. (d) HR-TEM image of ALD LNO-coated NCM811, showing the formation of a uniform coating layer. (e) Operando XANES spectra of TMs of bare and LNO-coated NCM, indicating suppressed transition metal reduction and enhanced structural stability with coating. Reproduced with permission from ref. 138. Copyright 2019, American Chemical Society.

figures.caption: Fig. 15 (a) Cross-sectional images of the interface between the uncoated and LiPON coated Li metal with sulfide SEs, showing improved interfacial contact and suppression of interfacial void formation with LiPON coating.
